# Settings reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-settings-docs.js — do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting below is reachable three ways, all of which go through the
same validation and the same apply pipeline:

- the dashboard, which builds its controls from this schema at runtime;
- `catwaf settings <group> field=value` — see [the CLI reference](cli.md#catwaf-settings);
- `PATCH /api/settings/<group>`.

A change is written, rendered into the Caddyfile, validated by Caddy, and
only then applied. If the result would not load, the previous
configuration is kept and the change is reported as rejected.

Fields marked _(secret)_ are write-only: they can be set, but are never
sent back to the browser or printed by the CLI.

Some settings depend on an optional Caddy module. When one is missing,
CatWAF **skips** that directive rather than emitting something Caddy would
reject and taking the site down with it — and reports the skip. Run
`catwaf doctor` to see what the installed build supports and what was left
out.

| [`headers`](#headers) | Response header policy, as named presets with per-header overrides. |
| [`cors`](#cors) | Cross-origin request rules applied at the WAF layer. |
| [`cookies`](#cookies) | Add missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags to backend cookies. |
| [`compression`](#compression) | gzip/zstd response compression, tradeable against CPU. |
| [`client_cache`](#client_cache) | Cache-Control and ETag policy for static assets. |
| [`html_injection`](#html_injection) | Insert a snippet into every HTML page without touching the app. |
| [`robots`](#robots) | Generate /robots.txt from your bot policy. |
| [`security_txt`](#security_txt) | Publish RFC 9116 vulnerability-reporting contact details. |
| [`error_pages`](#error_pages) | Replace the default error body for chosen status codes. |
| [`redirects`](#redirects) | Ordered redirect rules evaluated before the proxy target. |
| [`challenge`](#challenge) | Make ambiguous visitors prove they are a browser before passing them through. |
| [`ban_enforcement`](#ban_enforcement) | Check the local ban store on every request. Enabled automatically when an administrator adds a ban; requires the backend to be available. |
| [`bad_behavior`](#bad_behavior) | Ban an IP that generates too many error responses, even when no WAF rule fires. |
| [`client_probe`](#client_probe) | Check whether a suspicious client is itself an open proxy or relay. |
| [`tools_fingerprint`](#tools_fingerprint) | Score requests against known offensive tool signatures (sqlmap, nmap, nikto, gobuster, ...): an exact match bans the address, a close-but-uncertain match is challenged instead. Off by default — enabling it adds a runtime hop into CatWAF's API, which the protected site then depends on. |
| [`asn_lists`](#asn_lists) | Allow or block whole origin networks by AS number. |
| [`rdns_lists`](#rdns_lists) | Verify a crawler really belongs to the network it claims. |
| [`greylist`](#greylist) | Skip rate limiting and challenges for a known client, but keep the WAF watching it. |
| [`community_lists`](#community_lists) | Subscribe to maintained external lists and refresh them on a schedule. |
| [`dnsbl`](#dnsbl) | Check the client address against public abuse-source zones. |
| [`upload_scan`](#upload_scan) | Scan uploaded files with a local ClamAV daemon and refuse infected ones. |
| [`threat_network`](#threat_network) | Opt in to exchanging anonymised attacker signals with other CatWAF instances. |
| [`threat_feed`](#threat_feed) | Enforce CrowdSec Local API IP/range bans and CAPTCHA decisions, with bounded caching and configurable outage policy. |
| [`jobs`](#jobs) | The internal scheduler every time-based feature registers into. |
| [`backups`](#backups) | Copy configuration and data off the box on a schedule. |
| [`metrics`](#metrics) | Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint. |
| [`telemetry`](#telemetry) | Off unless you turn it on. Nothing is collected while this is disabled. |
| [`raw_config`](#raw_config) | Escape hatch for directives CatWAF does not model, by insertion context. |
| [`autoconf`](#autoconf) | Continuously apply configuration derived from container labels. |
| [`kubernetes`](#kubernetes) | Reconcile explicitly selected networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress resources using a namespace-scoped service account. |
| [`sites`](#sites) | Host registry and an explicit capacity limit for automatically managed sites. |
| [`cluster`](#cluster) | Optional external store for counters that must be consistent across nodes. |
| [`database`](#database) | Engine choice and pool tuning. SQLite is the right answer at Free's scale. |
| [`canary`](#canary) | Paths no legitimate visitor requests. Touching one is intent — probe it and the address is banned outright, before any payload is even evaluated. |
| [`edge_bans`](#edge_bans) | Render the newest active bans directly into the Caddyfile so banned addresses are dropped by Caddy itself — no forward_auth hop, no WAF evaluation, no bytes to the origin. |
| [`kernel_bans`](#kernel_bans) | Mirror active bans into an nftables set so banned addresses die at SYN, before Caddy. Requires CATWAF_KERNEL_BANS=1 in .env, root, nftables, and a one-time firewall rule you add yourself (catwaf kernel-bans print-rules). Host installs only. |
| [`ddos`](#ddos) | Under-attack switch: challenges every visitor (JavaScript proof), shortens cached verdicts to seconds, and keeps canary/edge/kernel enforcement at their most responsive. Connection timeouts live under Connections. |
| [`siem`](#siem) | Append every blocked request as JSON lines to data/siem.jsonl (rotated) and optionally POST batches to an HTTP collector. |
| [`alert_dispatch`](#alert_dispatch) | Actually send the alerts configured on the Alerts page: attack spikes, new bans and engine changes delivered to your webhooks or Telegram. |

## access

**Access control**

Host matching, method allowlist, deny behaviour and protocol limits.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reject_unknown_host` | switch | `false` | Serve a catch-all block that refuses any request whose Host header does not match a site CatWAF knows about. Closes the "reach the origin by IP" bypass. |
| `known_hosts` | list | _(empty)_ | Hostnames considered legitimate. Leave empty to derive from DOMAIN and the sites CatWAF has provisioned. |
| `unknown_host_action` | choice: `abort`, `status` | `abort` | "abort" closes the connection without a response; "status" returns the configured blocked status code. |
| `enforce_method_allowlist` | switch | `false` | Reject any method not on the list before the request is routed. Off by default so existing installs are unchanged. |
| `allowed_methods` | list | `GET, POST, HEAD, OPTIONS` | Allowed methods |
| `method_reject_status` | number (400–599) | `405` | Method rejection status |
| `blocked_status_code` | number (100–599) | `403` | What a denied request receives. 403 is the default; 404 hides the fact that a WAF is present. |
| `block_response_mode` | choice: `status`, `silent` | `status` | "silent" closes the connection without any response at all — invisible to fingerprinting tools, but a mistakenly blocked visitor also gets no explanation, which makes false positives much harder to diagnose. |
| `disable_plain_http` | switch | `false` | Do not listen on :80 at all, rather than listening and redirecting. A closed port is a smaller attack surface, but visitors typing http:// get a connection error instead of a redirect. |
| `waf_bypass_paths` | list | _(empty)_ | Requests matching these URI patterns skip Coraza/CRS inspection entirely — for webhook and upload endpoints that must receive raw bytes. Everything else stays protected. |
| `max_header_size_kb` | number (0–1024) | `0` | 0 leaves Caddy at its built-in default. |
| `max_body_size_mb` | number (0–10240) | `0` | 0 leaves the limit unset. Applies at the HTTP layer, before the WAF body limit. |
| `file_cache_size` | number (0–100000) | `0` | Only relevant when CatWAF serves files directly (static or PHP-FPM origin). 0 disables the cache. |

## mtls

**Mutual TLS**

Require a client certificate signed by your CA before serving anything.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | choice: `off`, `request`, `require`, `require_and_verify` | `off` | "require_and_verify" is real access control; "request" only asks for a certificate and still serves clients that do not present one. |
| `ca_pem` | multi-line text | _(unset)_ | Trusted CA certificate (PEM) |
| `verify_depth` | number (0–10) | `1` | Verification chain depth |
| `crl_pem` | multi-line text | _(unset)_ | Certificate revocation list (PEM) |

## real_ip

**Real client IP**

How CatWAF determines the client address when it sits behind another proxy.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Trust an upstream proxy for the client IP |
| `preset` | choice: `custom`, `cloudflare`, `private` | `custom` | "cloudflare" fills the trusted list from the Cloudflare edge ranges CatWAF already tracks; "private" trusts RFC1918 ranges. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list | _(empty)_ | Trusted proxy CIDRs |
| `header` | choice: `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`, `True-Client-IP`, `Forwarded` | `X-Forwarded-For` | Client IP header |
| `recursive` | switch | `true` | Resolve recursively through multiple hops |
| `proxy_protocol` | switch | `false` | For an L4/TCP load balancer in front of CatWAF that cannot set HTTP headers. Enabling this when nothing sends the PROXY header breaks every connection. |
| `proxy_protocol_allow` | list | _(empty)_ | PROXY protocol source CIDRs |

## tls

**TLS & certificates** · contains secrets

Certificate source, ACME behaviour and protocol/cipher strictness.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` | choice: `modern`, `intermediate`, `compatible` | `intermediate` | "modern" is TLS 1.3 only; "compatible" allows TLS 1.2 with a wider cipher list for legacy clients. |
| `cert_source` | choice: `acme`, `self-signed`, `custom` | `acme` | Certificate source |
| `self_signed_fallback` | switch | `true` | Serve a locally-issued certificate while DNS propagates, so the site is on HTTPS from the first request instead of plaintext or broken TLS. |
| `custom_cert_pem` | multi-line text | _(unset)_ | Certificate (PEM) |
| `custom_key_pem` | multi-line text | _(secret)_ | Private key (PEM) |
| `acme_provider` | choice: `letsencrypt`, `zerossl`, `custom` | `letsencrypt` | ACME provider |
| `acme_fallback` | switch | `false` | If the primary provider fails or is rate-limited, try the other one before giving up. |
| `acme_ca_url` | str | _(unset)_ | Custom ACME directory URL |
| `acme_email` | str | _(unset)_ | ACME account email |
| `acme_challenge` | choice: `http-01`, `tls-alpn-01`, `dns-01` | `http-01` | dns-01 is required for wildcard certificates and for origins that cannot be reached on :80. |
| `dns_provider` | choice: `none`, `cloudflare`, `route53`, `digitalocean`, `googleclouddns`, `azure`, `namecheap`, `gandi`, `porkbun`, `hetzner`, `linode`, `vultr`, `ovh`, `desec` | `none` | DNS provider (for dns-01) |
| `dns_api_token` | str | _(secret)_ | DNS provider API token |
| `wildcard` | switch | `false` | Request a wildcard certificate |
| `acme_retries` | number (0–10) | `3` | Issuance retry attempts |
| `acme_retry_delay_sec` | number (1–3600) | `30` | Delay between retries (seconds) |
| `ocsp_stapling` | switch | `true` | OCSP stapling |

## proxy

**Reverse proxy**

Protocol support, upstream verification, failover and caching.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `websockets` | choice: `allow`, `deny` | `allow` | Set to "deny" for a site that has no real-time features — an unexpected upgrade request is then rejected instead of tunnelled to the backend. |
| `protocol` | choice: `http`, `https`, `grpc` | `http` | Upstream protocol |
| `upstream_tls_verify` | switch | `false` | Off by default so existing self-signed backends keep working. Turn it on whenever the backend has a real certificate — otherwise a spoofed backend on the internal network is undetectable. |
| `upstream_ca_pem` | multi-line text | _(unset)_ | Upstream CA bundle (PEM) |
| `upstream_server_name` | str | _(unset)_ | Expected upstream server name (SNI) |
| `lb_policy` | choice: `round_robin`, `least_conn`, `first`, `ip_hash`, `random` | `round_robin` | Load-balancing policy |
| `retry_on` | list | _(empty)_ | Upstream response statuses that mark a backend unhealthy so the next one is tried: 5xx, 502, 503, 504. |
| `max_retries` | number (0–20) | `0` | Max retries (0 = Caddy default) |
| `retry_timeout_sec` | number (0–300) | `0` | Total retry budget (seconds, 0 = Caddy default) |
| `fail_duration_sec` | number (0–3600) | `0` | Mark an upstream down for (seconds, 0 = off) |
| `http2` | switch | `true` | HTTP/2 |
| `http3` | switch | `false` | Needs UDP on the same port to be open. Some corporate proxies mishandle HTTP/3, which is why this is opt-in. |
| `alt_svc_port` | number (0–65535) | `0` | Alt-Svc advertised port (0 = same port) |
| `auth_request_enabled` | switch | `false` | Delegate authorization to an external service |
| `auth_request_url` | str | _(unset)_ | Auth service address |
| `auth_request_uri` | str | `/auth` | Auth service URI |
| `auth_request_signin_url` | str | _(unset)_ | Sign-in redirect URL |
| `auth_request_copy_headers` | list | `Remote-User, Remote-Email` | Headers to copy from the auth response |
| `cache_enabled` | switch | `false` | Cache upstream responses |
| `cache_ttl_sec` | number (1–2592000) | `300` | Default cache TTL (seconds) |
| `cache_methods` | list | `GET, HEAD` | Cacheable methods |
| `cache_status_ttl` | rows | _(empty)_ | Per-status cache TTL |
| `cache_bypass_paths` | list | _(empty)_ | Never cache these paths |
| `cache_max_size_mb` | number (1–102400) | `512` | Cache size cap (MB) |

Each row of `cache_status_ttl` has:

| Column | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | number (–) | `200` |
| `ttl_sec` | number (–) | `300` |

| `permissions_policy` | str | _(unset)_ | Permissions-Policy |
| `referrer_policy` | choice: `(none)`, `no-referrer`, `no-referrer-when-downgrade`, `same-origin`, `origin`, `strict-origin`, `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `unsafe-url` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` | Referrer-Policy |
| `x_frame_options` | choice: `(none)`, `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN` | `SAMEORIGIN` | X-Frame-Options |
| `x_content_type_options` | switch | `true` | X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff |
| `x_dns_prefetch_control` | choice: `(none)`, `on`, `off` | _(unset)_ | X-DNS-Prefetch-Control |
| `coop` | choice: `(none)`, `unsafe-none`, `same-origin-allow-popups`, `same-origin` | _(unset)_ | Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy |
| `coep` | choice: `(none)`, `unsafe-none`, `require-corp`, `credentialless` | _(unset)_ | Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy |
| `corp` | choice: `(none)`, `same-site`, `same-origin`, `cross-origin` | _(unset)_ | Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy |
| `remove_headers` | list | `Server, X-Powered-By` | Headers to strip from responses |
| `custom` | rows | _(empty)_ | Custom response headers |

Each row of `custom` has:

| Column | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | _(unset)_ |
| `value` | str | _(unset)_ |
| `replace` | switch | `true` |

## cors

**CORS policy**

Cross-origin request rules applied at the WAF layer.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Enabled |
| `allow_origins` | list | _(empty)_ | Allowed origins |
| `allow_any_origin` | switch | `false` | Cannot be combined with credentials — the browser rejects "*" plus Allow-Credentials. |
| `allow_methods` | list | `GET, POST, OPTIONS` | Allowed methods |
| `allow_headers` | list | `Content-Type, Authorization` | Allowed request headers |
| `expose_headers` | list | _(empty)_ | Exposed response headers |
| `allow_credentials` | switch | `false` | Allow credentials |
| `max_age_sec` | number (0–86400) | `600` | Preflight cache (seconds) |
| `on_failure` | choice: `pass`, `deny` | `pass` | "pass" serves the request without CORS headers (the browser blocks it); "deny" refuses it outright at the edge. |

## challenge

**Challenge gate** · contains secrets

Make ambiguous visitors prove they are a browser before passing them through.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | choice: `off`, `cookie`, `javascript`, `captcha`, `provider` | `off` | "cookie" is the lightest tier; "captcha" is CatWAF's own generated image challenge; "provider" uses a third-party service. |
| `provider` | choice: `none`, `recaptcha`, `hcaptcha`, `turnstile`, `mcaptcha` | `none` | Third-party provider |
| `site_key` | str | _(unset)_ | Provider site key |
| `secret_key` | str | _(secret)_ | Provider secret key |
| `provider_verify_url` | str | _(unset)_ | Provider verify URL (mCaptcha/self-hosted) |

| `exempt_paths` | list | `/api/*, /.well-known/*` | Exempt paths |

| `captcha_length` | number (4–8) | `5` | Generated captcha length |
| `max_attempts` | number (1–20) | `5` | Attempts before the visitor is banned |

## ban_enforcement

**Runtime bans**

Check the local ban store on every request. Enabled automatically when an administrator adds a ban; requires the backend to be available.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Enforce runtime bans |

## bad_behavior

**Behavioural banning**

Ban an IP that generates too many error responses, even when no WAF rule fires.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Enabled |
| `window_sec` | number (10–86400) | `60` | Counting window (seconds) |
| `threshold` | number (1–10000) | `20` | Bad responses before a ban |
| `ban_seconds` | number (30–2592000) | `3600` | Ban duration (seconds) |
| `status_codes` | list | `400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 429, 500` | Status codes that count as bad |
| `count_waf_blocks` | switch | `true` | Count WAF blocks too |
| `escalate` | switch | `true` | Each subsequent ban for the same address doubles, up to the maximum below. |
| `max_ban_seconds` | number (60–31536000) | `86400` | Maximum ban length (seconds) |

## client_probe

**Client relay detection**

Check whether a suspicious client is itself an open proxy or relay.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Off by default on purpose: probing a client address costs request latency and can generate abuse reports against your server. Read the tradeoff before enabling. |
| `ports` | list | `3128, 8080, 1080, 9050, 8888` | Ports to probe |
| `timeout_ms` | number (50–5000) | `400` | Per-port timeout (ms) |
| `cache_minutes` | number (1–10080) | `1440` | Cache a verdict for (minutes) |
| `action` | choice: `flag`, `challenge`, `ban` | `flag` | Action on a positive result |
| `only_suspicious` | switch | `true` | Only probe already-suspicious clients |

## tools_fingerprint

**Scanner tool fingerprinting**

Score requests against known offensive tool signatures (sqlmap, nmap, nikto, gobuster, ...): an exact match bans the address, a close-but-uncertain match is challenged instead. Off by default — enabling it adds a runtime hop into CatWAF's API, which the protected site then depends on.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Enabled |
| `close_threshold` | number (0–100) | `55` | Similarity score (0-100) that counts as a close match |
| `ban_seconds` | number (60–2592000) | `86400` | Ban duration for an exact match (seconds) |
| `escalate` | switch | `true` | Each subsequent exact-match ban for the same address doubles, same as behavioural banning. |

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `allow` | list | _(empty)_ | Allowed ASNs |
| `block` | list | _(empty)_ | Blocked ASNs |
| `mode` | choice: `blocklist`, `allowlist` | `blocklist` | "allowlist" refuses every network except the allowed ones — very strict, and it will lock out any visitor whose ASN cannot be resolved. |

| `block_suffixes` | list | _(empty)_ | Blocked rDNS suffixes |
| `global_only` | switch | `true` | Skips the DNS round-trip for private and CGNAT ranges, which never have a useful PTR record. |
| `forward_confirm` | switch | `true` | Resolve the PTR name back to an address and require it to match. Without this, anyone controlling their own reverse DNS can claim to be Googlebot. |

| `timeout_ms` | number (100–10000) | `1500` | Lookup timeout (ms) |

## upload_scan

**Upload malware scanning**

Scan uploaded files with a local ClamAV daemon and refuse infected ones.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Requires a local clamd daemon. CatWAF does not install or bundle one; if it is missing, this feature reports itself unavailable. |
| `paths` | list | `/upload*` | Only these paths are routed through the scanner, so ordinary traffic is unaffected. |
| `methods` | list | `POST, PUT, PATCH` | Methods to scan |
| `max_scan_bytes` | number (1024–1073741824) | `26214400` | Bodies above this are handled by the oversize action rather than scanned, since buffering is bounded. |
| `oversize_action` | choice: `pass`, `block` | `pass` | Action for bodies too large to scan |
| `action` | choice: `block`, `flag` | `block` | Action when malware is found |
| `fail_open` | switch | `true` | On by default: a stopped clamd should not take uploads down. Turn off to refuse uploads that could not be scanned. |
| `timeout_ms` | number (500–120000) | `10000` | Scan timeout (ms) |
| `socket_path` | str | _(unset)_ | clamd socket path (blank = autodetect) |
| `host` | str | _(unset)_ | clamd TCP host (blank = use the socket) |
| `port` | number (1–65535) | `3310` | clamd TCP port |
| `ban_seconds` | number (0–2592000) | `0` | Ban the uploader for (seconds, 0 = do not ban) |

Paths no legitimate visitor requests. Touching one is intent — probe it and the address is banned outright, before any payload is even evaluated.

| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Enabled |
| `paths` | list | `/.env, /.git/config, /.git/HEAD, /.htpasswd, /.aws/credentials, /wp-config.php.bak` | Canary paths |
| `ban_seconds` | number (300–2592000) | `86400` | Ban duration (seconds) |
| `escalate` | switch | `true` | Escalate repeat offenders |

## edge_bans

**Edge ban enforcement** · advanced

Render the newest active bans directly into the Caddyfile so banned addresses are dropped by Caddy itself — no forward_auth hop, no WAF evaluation, no bytes to the origin.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Enabled |
| `max_rules` | number (50–2000) | `500` | Maximum rules rendered (newest first) |
| `include_cidrs` | switch | `true` | Include CIDR-range bans |
| `refresh_seconds` | number (15–600) | `30` | Refresh interval (seconds) |

## kernel_bans

**Kernel-level drops** · advanced

Mirror active bans into an nftables set so banned addresses die at SYN, before Caddy. Requires CATWAF_KERNEL_BANS=1 in .env, root, nftables, and a one-time firewall rule you add yourself (catwaf kernel-bans print-rules). Host installs only.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch | `false` | Enabled |
| `max_entries` | number (100–262144) | `65536` | Maximum set entries |

## ddos

**Anti-DDoS**

Under-attack switch: challenges every visitor (JavaScript proof), shortens cached verdicts to seconds, and keeps canary/edge/kernel enforcement at their most responsive. Connection timeouts live under Connections.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `emergency` | switch | `false` | UNDER-ATTACK MODE |
| `verdict_ttl_seconds` | number (1–20) | `2` | Verdict cache TTL while under attack (seconds) |
